headline: A 24% volume step-up lands cleanly, with easy-run HR dropping markedly against the prior block — pointing toward genuine aerobic adaptation rather than accumulated fatigue.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The shift from the prior four-week block into this one is notable not just for the volume increase but for what accompanied it: average heart rate on easy efforts dropped substantially despite more kilometres and more frequent sessions. That pattern — more load, lower HR at comparable efforts — is the direction you want adaptation to move, and it's worth naming clearly.

The lactate threshold reading from yesterday strengthens that picture. A threshold sitting at 4:24/km is consistent with a well-developed aerobic base, and the 20-week running streak (now matching your best) reflects the unbroken consistency underpinning it. This is not a week to second-guess the load — the physiological signals are coherent.

Strength frequency has held steady across both blocks, which matters given your hybrid profile. Maintaining that continuity through a volume step-up is a positive sign for overall load management.
watch_items: Monitor whether easy-run HR continues to trend downward or stabilises — further decline would confirm ongoing aerobic adaptation from this block.
Watch how back-to-back or near-daily run efforts feel subjectively as the streak extends; durability signals are as informative as pace or HR data at this point.
Track whether the volume step consolidates or continues rising — another large jump without a recovery week would shift the risk profile meaningfully.
Notice how strength quality holds through the higher running load — any degradation in session quality or capacity is worth flagging before it becomes a pattern.

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 155 km vs 125 km prior block (+24%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 144 bpm vs 157 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 8 vs 6 runs)
